climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

key.plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

key.plugboard: AN BY CF DR GJ HS IL KM PV QZ

limitations: Every result assumes UKW-B, the Army/Air Force wheels I-V and the 1940+ clear-Grundstellung indicator procedure.
One plaintext supplies every draw; each draw takes a different random stretch of it, so draws within a cell are not independent of the text's own letter frequencies.

Expected rank uses an analytic uniform-letter null (chi-square, 25 degrees of freedom, Wilson-Hilferty) because 500 empirical null trials cannot reach a one-in-two-million tail. The artifact records the empirical null mean and sd beside the analytic ones so the model can be checked.

The ranked population is one indicator ordering's 1,054,560 daily keys treated as independent wrong keys. Neighbouring settings share partial decryptions, so the true rank can differ; the figure is the rank against that many independent draws.

This calibrates a single message's IC. The indicator sweep pooled the three messages of the date (371 letters), which the 371-letter row stands in for; pooling across separately keyed messages is not identical to one 371-letter message.
hypothesis: Averaged over 32 key draws per cell, the true rotor setting's unsteckered index of coincidence under a ten-pair stecker would be retained in the top 200 of the 1,054,560 daily keys its own indicator ordering ranks with mean probability below 5% at 167 letters and at 371 letters, while with no stecker it is retained with mean probability above 95% at 167 letters. This replaces the single-draw, z >= 3 criterion of phase1-stecker-calibration-v1 (review 2026-10-02, P5).
refuted_by: A ten-pair mean retention probability of 5% or more at 167 or at 371 letters, or a zero-pair mean retention probability of 95% or less at 167 letters.

ic_rank_calibration.rationale: The indicator sweep runs each indicator ordering separately: 60 wheel orders x 17,576 ring settings = 1,054,560 daily keys ranked by pooled IC over the date's 371 letters, top 200 kept, before the next ordering. The true key competes only within its own ordering's arm. A ranking stage is usable only if the true key lands in that retained list, which is a statement about the extreme of a million wrong keys, not about z >= 3 against 400 of them. Corrected after the first run from 2,109,120, which counted both orderings as one ranking (PR #10 review).
